description_full: Autohome Inc. operates as an online destination for automobile consumers in the People's Republic of China. The company delivers interactive content and tools to automobile consumers through its websites, autohome.com.cn, che168.com, and ttpai.cn on PCs, mobile devices, mobile applications, and mini apps. It also provides media services, including automaker advertising services and regional marketing campaigns; and leads generation services comprising dealer subscription services, advertising services for individual dealers, and used automobile listing and other platform-based services. In addition, the company offers Autohome Mall, an online transaction platform; and online bidding platform for used automobiles, as well as collects commissions for facilitating transactions of auto-financing and insurance products on its platform. The company was formerly known as Sequel Limited and changed its name to Autohome Inc. in October 2011. Autohome Inc. was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $13K ranks in the bottom quartile among Communication Services peers, declining at 12%/yr — weakening productivity. Each employee generates $31K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $9K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Autohome Inc. is a mid-cap communication services business with a $2.6B market cap on $49M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -65% over the past three years and -22% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +15.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 72% against a 9% cost of capital — a 63-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 86% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $116M in free cash flow — roughly 237 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.62×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 14.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 67% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 11.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 236% operating margin runs 227pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 11.51x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-35.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 15% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 9% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 0.84, it moves roughly with the market.
About $9.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 30% in the 2020 crash and 42% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 35% below its DCF fair value of $35.39, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 18%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $33.61 to $37.81 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Communication Services peers: P/E 24.9 vs 14.9 and P/FCF 22.8 vs 11.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 31% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.4% (below the risk-free rate).
The 12 covering analysts target $21.25 on average, 7% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 72% clears the cost of capital of 9.0% by 63pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.58).
It runs a 86% gross margin and converts 237% of revenue into free cash flow, or 168% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only 0.62x.
ROE of 6% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.2x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 74pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 335.8% of revenue on R&D and 69.1% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.9B (104% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
The Beneish M-score (-1.93) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -64.7% over 3 years, -48.5% over 5 years and -22.1% over 10 years, so the decline is deepening, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 53%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -24.7% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 36.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.3%), and institutions hold 45%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (10 sales, net $606K sold).
It returns 14.4% a year to shareholders (6.0% in buybacks and 8.1% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 0.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It pays out 274% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 3,785 employees, each generates about $13K of revenue, 0.0x the Communication Services median, and productivity has fallen 11.6% a year.
That works out to $31K of free cash flow per employee.
